title: Progress needs recovery
objective: For EventuallyDispatched and EventuallyAcked under a stated fairness and crash assumption, give the lasso that refutes the property or answer "none", and say which assumption each property needs.

blocks.md: In the time stage you checked that a hold eventually resolves under weak fairness, and wrote it as CL-5.3. Crashes now join that model. Before you read on, decide which part of that claim cracks, and keep your answer.

choice.prompt: A check of "every committed command is eventually acknowledged" passes. Its configuration has no Crash action. What did it establish about your system with crashes?

options.text: The property holds with crashes too, because the check passed.
options.why: Crashes were outside the model, so the check is silent about them.

options.text: It holds if crashes are rare, since the check passed without any.
options.why: The model has no notion of rare. One crash at the wrong moment is a behavior.

options.text: Nothing about crashes: they are NOT COVERED [N].
options.why: A model without an action cannot speak about behaviors that need it.

blocks.md: The outbox has two progress properties. `EventuallyDispatched` says a committed command leads to a request. `EventuallyAcked` says it leads to an acknowledgement. Each is checked under fairness you state. A refutation is a lasso: a stem, then a cycle that breaks no stated fairness conjunct and never reaches the goal.
Crashes on, at most two. The worker's actions and the provider's are weakly fair, and Recover has no fairness.
blocks.direction: Check asserts: EventuallyAcked holds on every behavior that satisfies the fairness. A violation is a lasso that satisfies it and never acknowledges.

code.text:
WorkerFair   == \A c \in Cmds : /\ WF_vars(Dispatch(c)) /\ WF_vars(Receive(c))
                                /\ WF_vars(Persist(c))  /\ WF_vars(Ack(c))
ProviderFair == WF_vars(\E r \in reqs : Accept(r))
LiveSpec     == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WorkerFair /\ ProviderFair

EventuallyDispatched == \A c \in Cmds : (c \in committed) ~> (attempts[c] > 0)
EventuallyAcked      == \A c \in Cmds : (c \in committed) ~> (status[c] = "acked")
\* Here: MaxCrashes = 2

options.text: Holds: weak fairness keeps the worker going.
options.why: Fairness applies to enabled actions. A crashed worker has none, and nothing obliges Recover.
Stuttering after a crash is a behavior, and the lasso is fair to every stated action.

blocks.after: The lasso ends with a crash, then the worker down and stuttering, and the lasso checker accepts it as fair. With the crash actions switched off, the same property passes {{run:RUN-tlc-crash-liveness}}. That is specimen SP-8.6: a liveness check that passes only because the model left crashes out. Compare with the answer you kept. CL-5.3's check still passes on its own model. What cracks is the assumption that the worker keeps running, SEAM-8: an assumption record.

blocks.md: Crashes unlimited, with no bound on sends. Recover is now weakly fair too.
blocks.direction: Check asserts: EventuallyAcked holds on every behavior that satisfies the fairness.

code.text:
RecoverFair == WF_vars(Recover)
LiveSpec2   == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WorkerFair /\ ProviderFair /\ RecoverFair
\* Here: MaxCrashes = -1, which means no bound on crashes

options.text: Holds: the worker always comes back.
options.why: It comes back and crashes again before acting. Weak fairness needs an action continuously enabled, and each crash disables Dispatch.

options.text: It would hold with strong fairness on Recover.
options.why: Recover is already enabled the whole time the worker is down, so strong fairness on it changes nothing. Dispatch is the starved action.

options.text: Violated by a crash and recover cycle.
options.why: The cycle is fair to every stated action, yet Dispatch never fires.

blocks.after: Weak fairness cannot see an action that is enabled only between a recovery and the next crash.

blocks.md: Crashes unlimited. The worker's actions are now strongly fair; Recover and the provider stay weakly fair.
blocks.direction: Check asserts: EventuallyAcked holds on every behavior that satisfies the fairness.

code.text:
WorkerStrong == \A c \in Cmds : /\ SF_vars(Dispatch(c)) /\ SF_vars(Receive(c))
                                /\ SF_vars(Persist(c))  /\ SF_vars(Ack(c))
LiveSpec3    == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WorkerStrong /\ ProviderFair /\ RecoverFair
\* Here: MaxCrashes = -1

options.why: Strong fairness takes an action enabled infinitely often, so some window between a recovery and the next crash is eventually used.

options.text: Violated by a crash and recover cycle.
options.why: That cycle starved weak fairness only.

blocks.after: There are two honest ways to say that the worker recovers: crashes eventually stop (a finite budget, with Recover fair), or the worker's actions get strong fairness. Write yours as an assumption. The provider's recovery is a separate assumption, needed for EventuallyAcked only. Provider idempotency serves safety, not progress.

blocks.md:
Worked example: EventuallyDispatched needs a worker that recovers and nothing from the provider, so its fairness is `WorkerFair` plus recovery. Write the fairness that EventuallyAcked needs, then compare it with the table. Safety needs no fairness at all.

| Property | Kind | The worker recovers | The provider replies | Provider idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NoLostIntent | safety | no | no | no |
| NoDoubleCharge | safety | no | no | yes, one key per intent |
| EventuallyDispatched | liveness | yes | no | no |
| EventuallyAcked | liveness | yes | yes | no |

choice.prompt: EventuallyDispatched. Crashes are unlimited, Recover is weakly fair, and the worker's actions are weakly fair. Which lasso refutes it, or is there none?

options.text: Commit, then Crash and Recover forever: the worker is never up long enough to Dispatch.
options.why: Dispatch is enabled only while the worker is up, so weak fairness does not force it, and the cycle is fair to Recover.

options.text: None: weak fairness forces Dispatch because the intent stays pending.
options.why: Weak fairness forces an action only if it stays enabled. Each crash disables Dispatch.

options.text: Commit, Crash, then stutter forever with the worker down.
options.why: Recover is weakly fair and stays enabled while the worker is down, so this lasso breaks a stated conjunct.

choice.prompt: EventuallyAcked. Crashes are finite, Recover and the worker's actions are weakly fair, and the provider has no fairness. Is there a fair cycle that never acknowledges?

options.text: No: the worker's weak fairness forces the acknowledgement of every stored result.
options.why: The worker cannot acknowledge a result the provider never sent.

options.text: No: a finite crash budget brings the worker back, and that is enough.
options.why: A finite budget recovers the worker. It does not make the provider answer.

options.text: Yes: the provider never replies, and the worker waits and stutters.
options.why: Nothing obliges the provider to act, and the stuttering cycle breaks no stated conjunct.
